- When sentiment is negative and forecast is trending down, model tends to underestimate future prices — correct by adding 1–2% to forecast for mean reversion bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and overcorrects — reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection lag.
- If sentiment is positive and forecast is flat or slightly rising, model underestimates upside — increase forecast by 1–2% for sentiment-driven momentum.
- Model consistently underpredicts true outcomes in early horizon (1–3 days) when sentiment is volatile — apply a 0.5–1.5% upward bias for short-term volatility.
- When sentiment turns from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast at sentiment crossover point to capture sentiment shift.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate mean price — apply 1–2% downward adjustment if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
